problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a circuit for its fleet of autonomous drones to inspect nine critical communication hubs, each positioned at specific grid coordinates. The hubs are labeled as follows:

Hub Alpha: Grid position (78,29)
Hub Beta: Grid position (37,109)
Hub Gamma: Grid position (144,108)
Hub Delta: Grid position (21,26)
Hub Epsilon: Grid position (106,16)
Hub Zeta: Grid position (25,106)
Hub Eta: Grid position (198,39)
Hub Theta: Grid position (187,7)
Hub Iota: Grid position (114,110)

The flight distances between hubs, measured in kilometers, are precisely known:
Alpha to Gamma: 102.9 km
Alpha to Delta: 57.1 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 30.9 km
Alpha to Zeta: 93.5 km
Alpha to Eta: 120.4 km
Alpha to Theta: 111.2 km
Alpha to Iota: 88.6 km
Beta to Gamma: 107.0 km
Beta to Delta: 84.5 km
Beta to Epsilon: 115.8 km
Beta to Zeta: 12.4 km
Beta to Eta: 175.6 km
Beta to Theta: 181.4 km
Beta to Iota: 77.0 km
Gamma to Delta: 147.8 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 99.5 km
Gamma to Zeta: 119.0 km
Gamma to Eta: 87.6 km
Gamma to Theta: 109.8 km
Gamma to Iota: 30.1 km
Delta to Epsilon: 85.6 km
Delta to Zeta: 80.1 km
Delta to Eta: 177.5 km
Delta to Theta: 167.1 km
Delta to Iota: 125.3 km
Epsilon to Zeta: 121.1 km
Epsilon to Eta: 94.8 km
Epsilon to Theta: 81.5 km
Epsilon to Iota: 94.3 km
Zeta to Eta: 185.5 km
Zeta to Theta: 189.9 km
Zeta to Iota: 89.1 km
Eta to Theta: 33.8 km
Eta to Iota: 110.0 km
Theta to Iota: 126.2 km

Due to permanent signal interference, a direct flight corridor between Hub Alpha and Hub Beta is unavailable. Furthermore, a regulatory protocol mandates that exactly one of the following two flight paths must be incorporated into the inspection circuit: the corridor between Hub Beta and Hub Gamma, or the corridor between Hub Gamma and Hub Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient flight circuit, minimizing total distance traveled, such that each hub is inspected exactly once before the drone returns to its origin hub.
